html:
The Ho-Chunk, long called the Winnebago, are a Siouan-speaking people of what is now Wisconsin, living around Green Bay and Lake Winnebago among Algonquian neighbours such as the Menominee.

In 1634 the French explorer Jean Nicolet met them at Green Bay. Soon after, epidemics and a war with the Illinois cut their numbers sharply. They recovered, farmed maize, and took part in the fur trade. By their tradition the Otoe, Iowa and Missouria once split off from them.

In the 1800s they lost their land through treaties, and some fought in the Black Hawk War of 1832. The US moved them again and again, to Iowa, Minnesota, South Dakota and Nebraska. Many returned to Wisconsin on their own. Today there are two tribes, the Ho-Chunk Nation of Wisconsin and the Winnebago Tribe of Nebraska.
